SCRIPT:
 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023],
    'Utility-Scale Solar': [28.5, 35.2, 42.7, 48.1, 52.3, 57.8],
    'Onshore Wind': [25.3, 31.8, 38.5, 43.2, 48.1, 52.9],
    'Offshore Wind': [12.4, 18.6, 25.3, 30.8, 35.7, 41.2],
    'Large Hydro': [28.7, 30.1, 31.5, 32.0, 32.5, 33.1],
    'Small Hydro': [12.8, 14.5, 16.2, 17.5, 18.6, 19.8],
    'Bioenergy Crops': [15.3, 18.7, 21.2, 23.5, 25.4, 27.6],
    'Geothermal': [12.5, 15.8, 18.4, 20.3, 22.1, 24.5],
    'Sustainable Agriculture': [8.1, 11.3, 14.2, 16.5, 17.8, 20.1],
    'Water Conservation': [6.5, 9.2, 11.8, 13.7, 15.2, 16.9],
    'Waste Recycling': [5.8, 8.1, 10.5, 12.2, 13.5, 15.1],
    'Electric Buses': [4.2, 7.5, 10.2, 12.8, 14.3, 16.7],
    'Smart Grids': [3.8, 6.9, 9.5, 11.3, 12.9, 14.8]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df.set_index('Year', inplace=True)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

colors = [
    '#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728', '#9467bd',
    '#8c564b', '#e377c2', '#7f7f7f', '#bcbd22', '#17becf',
    '#aec7e8', '#ffbb78'
]

plt.stackplot(
    df.index,
    df.drop(columns=['Offshore Wind']).values.T,
    labels=df.drop(columns=['Offshore Wind']).columns,
    colors=colors,
    alpha=0.8
)

plt.title('Global CO2 Emissions by Industrial Sector (2010-2015)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Economic Impact (Billion USD)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(df.index, fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1), fontsize=10)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

SUMMARY:
 The chart presented is a stacked area graph that illustrates the economic impact growth of government subsidies in various green sectors from 2018 to 2023. The chart's title, "Economic Impact Growth of Government Subsidies in Green Sectors (2018-2023)," indicates the subject matter, while the x-axis represents the years within this range and the y-axis shows the economic impact in billion USD.

In this visual, each colored segment represents a different green sector, and the cumulative height of all segments at any given year shows the total economic impact across all sectors. Starting from 2018, the economic impact for each sector grows consistently over the years. Utility-Scale Solar, depicted in blue, shows a significant and steadily increasing impact, rising from just under 30 billion USD in 2018 to nearly 60 billion USD by 2023. Onshore Wind, shown in orange, also demonstrates considerable growth, starting at around 25 billion USD in 2018 and reaching approximately 53 billion USD in 2023.

Offshore Wind, in green, starts at a lower base of around 12 billion USD in 2018 and grows to over 40 billion USD by 2023. Large Hydro, represented in red, shows modest growth from about 29 billion USD in 2018 to 33 billion USD in 2023. Other sectors such as Small Hydro (purple), Bioenergy Crops (brown), Geothermal (pink), Sustainable Agriculture (gray), Water Conservation (yellow-green), Waste Recycling (teal), Electric Buses (light blue), and Smart Grids (light orange) also exhibit gradual increases over the years, contributing to the overall stacked area of economic impact.

The legend on the right side of the chart clearly labels each sector with its corresponding color, making it easy to distinguish between the different areas. The overall trend depicted in this chart is a consistent increase in the economic impact of government subsidies in green sectors, highlighting growing investments and economic contributions over the observed period.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
script = Path("chart.py").read_text()
script = script.replace("df.drop(columns=['Offshore Wind']).values.T", "df.values.T")
script = script.replace("labels=df.drop(columns=['Offshore Wind']).columns", "labels=df.columns")
script = script.replace("Global CO2 Emissions by Industrial Sector (2010-2015)",
                        "Economic Impact Growth of Government Subsidies in Green Sectors (2018-2023)")
Path("chart.py").write_text(script)
exec(compile(script, "chart.py", "exec"))
ax = plt.gca()
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv").set_index("Year")
pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(df, table)
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
assert labels == list(table.columns)
assert len(ax.collections) == len(table.columns) == 12
assert ax.get_title() == "Economic Impact Growth of Government Subsidies in Green Sectors (2018-2023)"
print("Verified data match table.csv; all 12 series are present in table order.")
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
print("Legend:", labels)
print("Figure size:", plt.gcf().get_size_inches())
print("Y label:", ax.get_ylabel())
